task_desc: Test the gate when the secret key is not configured. The gate (run_experiment.py --record E-XXX.md --run '<cmd>') must fail closed: without a gate key (BMAD_GATE_KEY env or ~/.bmad/gate-key), it must NOT write an APPROVED decision — it reports that the gate key is missing and the record stays undecided. A missing key must never produce a fake approval.

Test the gate's --dry-run mode. Running 'run_experiment.py --record E-XXX.md --run "<cmd>" --dry-run' must PREVIEW the decision (measured value, threshold comparison, would-be GATE-OK token) WITHOUT writing anything to the record. The record must remain untouched after a dry-run. Format checks must always use --dry-run, never a real --run.

Test the gate's free-zone bench rejection. A measurement command that executes a script inside a free zone (scratch/, tmp/, temp/) — e.g. 'python3 scratch/bench.py' — must be REJECTED before execution: the gate requires the measurement script itself to live under methodology protection, so a bench in a free zone cannot produce an approval. The gate must refuse with an error and write no decision.

Test the gate's metric cross-check. When the measurement command produces a metric whose name differs from the hypothesis claim's metric (e.g. claim names 'accuracy' but the run reports 'latency'), the gate must write a MISMATCH metric note and the approval must NOT unlock code — a metric redefinition is an ADVISORY-BLOCK.
